title: Prove retained follow-up context in Node Vitest

intentCoverage.report:
# Dough Intent Coverage

**Verdict: Caught.**

On a continuation after the source record is gone, the retry's sent text omitted the recorded source context. The maintained equality that requires that context and then the instruction failed.

**Next proof action.** None for this omission on the continuation path these two specs exercise. The caller owns any further routing. This probe does not choose a repair.

## Story and revision

- Story: SEED-413#prove-follow-up-context-on-vitest, `.planning/seeds/SEED-413-renovate-dashboard-unit-tests.md#prove-follow-up-context-on-vitest`.
- Plan: `.planning/slice-plans/850-prove-follow-up-context-on-vitest/PLAN.md`, slices 5 and 7.
- Revision: `76b599da18dca0da2499f87944e2c6020f4f0807` ("Record that the follow-up context proofs match the story.").
- Scratch checkout: `/tmp/dough-ic-SEED-413-follow-up`, a detached shared clone of that revision. `node_modules` was a clonefile copy from the execution worktree (separate inode). Pre-probe `git status --porcelain` was empty. Node v24.21.0. The execution worktree was not edited and remained at the same revision with an empty status.

## Promise

Kept as suggested. The story goal says the receiving agent is sent the source context, the developer's request, and the reporting context, in that order, and that a retry still sends them after the source record is gone. The retry examples in the story and in slices 5 and 7 say the saved context and the instruction are sent once after the source is gone.

The equalities that failed require the recorded source context and then the instruction. The Dashboard reporting block is the third segment in the first-send session-input proof, which this command does not run.

## Fault

One edit, fixtures and assertions left intact, in `dashboard/server/launchAttemptAdmit.ts`. `admitAttempt` still keeps and admits the saved attempt. When the call is a continuation (`continued` is set), the request passed to the run drops `followUp.context` and keeps the instruction.

## Checks and observations

Command, unchanged for baseline, fault, and restoration:

```sh
npm run test:dashboard:backend -- launches/agent-launch-follow-up-continuation.spec.ts launches/agent-launch-follow-up-attempt-identity.spec.ts --workers=1
```

Baseline: 8 passed, exit 0. `/usr/bin/time -p` real 3.17 s. Vitest Duration 2.08 s.

Fault run: 5 failed, 3 passed, exit 1. `/usr/bin/time -p` real 2.12 s. Vitest Duration 1.54 s.

Reach on the source-gone path: the second accept still returned `accepted`, and the kept attempt id and acceptance time still matched, before the sent-text equality failed. For the story continuation, the catalog read stayed at 1, so the retry did not read the source again.

Wrong behavior, from the assertion diff: the continuation input was `Continue\n\nTaken story: SEED-A#a`. The recorded session context was absent, including the preamble, the session facts, and the final report. The instruction `Continue` was present. With the saved context missing, `unattachedInput` also appended the Taken-story label.

The assertion that caught it is `sentOnce` in `dashboard/backend-tests/launches/agent-launch-follow-up-attempt-identity.spec.ts` at the `expect(input).toBe([context, instruction].join("\n\n"))` call, reached from "repeating a retained follow-up after the source record is removed resumes it with the saved context". The same omission failed `expect(text).toBe([context, instruction].join("\n\n"))` in `agent-launch-follow-up-continuation.spec.ts` in "continues a kept follow-up after the source record is removed". The story continuations failed `expect(resumed[1]?.input).toBe(recoverContext)` and `expect(run.input).toContain("No session context is retained.")`. Their received text was the instruction plus a Taken-story label, and the story context was absent.

The same continuation edit also failed "is resumed by repeating the same follow-up", where the source record was still present. The claim is the continuation run these specs exercise, including the run after the source record is removed. The pending Codex recovery and the legacy story builder call passed; they do not go through this continuation run.

## Restoration

The original `launchAttemptAdmit.ts` was copied back. Its SHA-256 matched the pre-fault file `53be56951bfd5975affc50dbfcb37f4e5bc9a0d9181abd9ccc329e36177bd497`. `git diff` and `git status --porcelain` were empty. The same command then passed 8 tests, exit 0. `/usr/bin/time -p` real 1.55 s. Vitest Duration 1.10 s. Test reports under `dashboard/backend-tests/test-results/` stayed ignored.

## Prior disposition

Plan 850 defers process review to wrap-up and asks for this Dough Intent Coverage check because the story replaced the Playwright follow-up specs. That is the request for this probe. It is not a recorded repair for this promise, and this result does not open one.

## Cost

- **Test runtime.** 6.84 s measured, the sum of `/usr/bin/time -p` real for the same command: baseline 3.17 s, fault 2.12 s, restored 1.55 s. Vitest Duration for those runs was 2.08 s, 1.54 s, and 1.10 s.
- **Human effort.** Unavailable. No separate human-time record was taken.
- **Agent effort.** Unavailable. No separate agent-duration or token measure was recorded.


- **Invocation-to-report elapsed.** 772106 ms (measured), from 1795741096000 to 1795741868106 in Unix epoch ms. The end clock was sampled after writing the prepared report body.

## Wrap-up disposition

Checked revision `76b599da18dca0da2499f87944e2c6020f4f0807`. Verdict: Caught. No follow-up.
